Summary: After seventy years in Babylon, God kept his promise and brought his people home: Cyrus decreed it, Zerubbabel led it, and Ezra and Nehemiah rebuilt what exile had broken. The return was joyful yet incomplete: the people were home but still waiting for a greater deliverance. That longing points to Christ, whose return from the grave and promised return in glory will end every exile for good.
